mainTopic: Temple music: the מגריפה, who the musicians were, and the Torah sources for the Levites' שירה
overview: The amud finishes describing the מגריפה, a Temple instrument. It gives two versions: one says the instrument made one hundred tones, and a ברייתא says one thousand. רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory aid: the ברייתא is the one that exaggerates. The גמרא then explains the משנה's dispute about who the Temple musicians were. Everyone agrees the voice is the main part of the song. The real question is what serving on the דוכן proves about a person's lineage and his right to מעשרות. Next, a ברייתא brings a dispute about whether a קרבן is valid without the Levites' song. רבי מאיר says it is not valid, and the חכמים say it is. Finally, many sages bring different פסוקים as the Torah source for the duty of שירה, and רב מתנה adds that ביכורים also need song. The last source, from חנניא, is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: The מגריפה had ten holes making one hundred tones
steps.stepSummary: The description of the מגריפה continues: ten holes, each making ten tones, for a total of one hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: It had ten holes. Each hole made ten kinds of tone. So the whole instrument made one hundred kinds of tone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a description of the מגריפה, a musical instrument in the מקדש. It gives the math of how many sounds it could make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues a statement that began just before this section. Ten holes times ten tones each gives one hundred tones. Remember this number, because the next step gives a bigger one.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of tone or musical sound
It turns out; it comes out that

phrases.english: There were ten holes in it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the מגריפה, the Temple instrument being described just before this.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מוֹצִיא עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר,
phrases.english: each and every one produced ten kinds of tone,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת כּוּלָּהּ מוֹצִיאָה מֵאָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר.
phrases.english: so it turns out the whole instrument produced one hundred kinds of tone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the מגריפה from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגריפה had ten holes, each producing ten tones, for one hundred tones in total.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the מגריפה with one thousand tones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the instrument's size and says each hole made one hundred tones, for one thousand in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: It was one אמה wide and one אמה tall, and a handle stuck out of it. It had ten holes, and each made one hundred kinds of tone. So the whole instrument made one thousand kinds of tone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes the same instrument, but with a much larger number of tones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the instrument's size and its handle. The big change is the number: one hundred tones per hole instead of ten, so one thousand in total instead of one hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of about an arm's length

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
It was one cubit wide and one cubit tall,
and a handle stuck out of it,
and there were ten holes in it,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד מוֹצִיא מֵאָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר,
phrases.english: each one produced one hundred kinds of tone,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת כּוּלָּהּ מוֹצִיאָה אֶלֶף מִינֵי זֶמֶר.
phrases.english: so it turns out the whole instrument produced one thousand kinds of tone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same description, with larger numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, each of the ten holes produced one hundred tones, for one thousand in total.

steps.title: A memory aid: the ברייתא exaggerates
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a way to remember which version has the bigger number: the ברייתא exaggerates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory aid is that the ברייתא exaggerates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a simple trick to remember which version said one hundred and which said one thousand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions with different numbers, and it is easy to mix them up. The trick is that the ברייתא tends to exaggerate, so the bigger number (one thousand) belongs to the ברייתא. The smaller number (one hundred) belongs to the earlier statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Your memory aid; a sign to help you remember

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier statement says the מגריפה made one hundred tones. The ברייתא says one thousand. The trick to remember this: the ברייתא exaggerates.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And your memory aid: the baraita exaggerates.
phrases.notes: He means the bigger number, one thousand, is the ברייתא's, since it tends to exaggerate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the two versions with a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To remember the two versions: the ברייתא is the one that exaggerates, so it has one thousand tones.

steps.title: Suggestion: the dispute is whether song is mainly voice or instruments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about who the musicians were and suggests the dispute is about the main part of Temple song.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They were slaves of כהנים,' and so on. Let us say this is what they disagree about. The one who says they were slaves thinks the main part of the song is singing with the mouth, and the instruments are only there to make the sound sweeter. The one who says they were לויים thinks the main part of the song is the instruments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's dispute about who played the instruments in the מקדש. It suggests a reason for the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the voice is the main part, the instruments are just background, so even slaves can play them. If the instruments are the main part, they are part of the Temple song itself, which is the job of the לויים. This is only a suggestion, and the next step will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא will test)
The main part of the Temple song

steps.confusionAlert: There are three views in the משנה: slaves of כהנים, Israelites of pure lineage (רבי יוסי), and לויים. This suggestion only explains two of them. That missing middle view is exactly what the next step attacks.

phrases.english: The mishna says: "And they were slaves of priests," and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's dispute about who the Temple musicians were. "And so on" points to the other views there.

phrases.english: Let us say they disagree about this:
that the one who says they were slaves holds:
the main part of the song is with the mouth,
and the instrument is only there to sweeten the sound,
and the one who says they were Levites holds:
the main part of the song is with the instrument!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's dispute about the musicians.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: whoever says slaves holds the voice is the main part of the song; whoever says לויים holds the instruments are the main part.

steps.title: Challenge: this does not explain רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this suggestion can explain רבי יוסי, who says the musicians were Israelites of pure lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? What does רבי יוסי hold? If he holds the main part of song is with the mouth, slaves should be enough. If he holds the main part of song is with the instrument, we need לויים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion. It shows the suggestion has no room for רבי יוסי's middle view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the suggestion, there are only two options. If the voice is the main part, slaves would be fine, so why require Israelites of pure lineage? If the instruments are the main part, only לויים would work, so ordinary Israelites would not be enough. Either way, רבי יוסי's view makes no sense, so the suggestion must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? (it opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Can you really think so?
What does Rabbi Yosei hold?
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי is the view in the משנה that the musicians were Israelites of pure family lineage.

phrases.english: If he holds the main part of song is with the mouth,
then slaves are enough,
and if he holds the main part of song is with the instrument,
then we need Levites!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the dispute is about whether song is mainly voice or instruments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That two-way split leaves no reason for רבי יוסי's requirement of Israelites of pure lineage. Either slaves would be enough, or only לויים would work.

steps.title: Answer: everyone agrees song is mainly voice; the dispute is about what the platform proves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי holds the voice is the main part. The real dispute is whether serving on the דוכן proves a person's lineage and his right to tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds the main part of song is with the mouth. Here they disagree about whether we raise someone from the platform to the status of pure lineage and to receiving מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first suggestion and gives the real reason for the dispute. It is about what we can learn about someone from seeing him serve on the musicians' platform.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All agree the voice is the main part, so the instruments are not the issue. The question is whether seeing someone on the דוכן is proof of his family status. That could mean proof that he has pure lineage, which matters for marriage. It could even mean proof that he is a לוי, which matters for receiving מעשרות. The three views in the משנה match different answers to this question.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (it keeps the original view and explains it differently)
We raise someone to a status, meaning we treat him as having it
The platform where the Temple musicians and singers stood
Pure family lineage, which matters for marriage
Tithes, here the tithe given to לויים

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute in the משנה is not about voice versus instruments. Everyone agrees the voice is the main part. The dispute is about what serving on the דוכן proves: nothing, pure lineage, or even לוי status for tithes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that serving in the מקדש could be treated as evidence of a family's status. Such evidence matters for marriage and for who may receive מעשרות.

phrases.english: Actually, he holds the main part of song is with the mouth,
and here they disagree about whether we raise someone from the platform
phrases.notes: The דוכן is the platform where the musicians stood. "Raise" means we treat the person as having proven status.

phrases.english: to pure lineage and to tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by moving the dispute to a different question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the dispute to a different question, so רבי יוסי's view now makes sense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the תנאים disagreed about whether the voice or the instruments are the main part of Temple song.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree the voice is the main part. They disagree about whether serving on the דוכן proves pure lineage, and even לוי status for receiving מעשרות.

steps.title: Matching each view of the musicians to a rule about the platform
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the three views. Slaves: the דוכן proves nothing. Levites: it proves both lineage and the right to tithes. Israelites: it proves lineage but not the right to tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the musicians were slaves holds that serving on the platform does not raise a person to the status of good lineage, and does not give him a right to tithes. The one who says they were Levites holds that it raises him both to good lineage and to receiving tithes. The one who says they were Israelites holds that it raises him to good lineage but not to receiving tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it began in step 6. It shows how each of the three opinions in the משנה matches a different view about what serving on the דוכן proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the real argument is about what the דוכן proves, and here the three views are lined up. If slaves could serve, serving proves nothing. If only Levites served, serving proves you are a Levite, so you get tithes too. If Israelites of pure lineage served, serving proves good family, but not that you are a Levite, so you get no tithes.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not raise someone to a status; the platform proves nothing

steps.whatToRemember: Three views, three levels. Slaves: the דוכן proves nothing. Israelites: it proves lineage only. Levites: it proves lineage and the right to tithes.
steps.confusionAlert: The Israelite view still says the musicians had pure lineage. It just means serving on the דוכן doesn't prove someone is a Levite, so it can't give him tithes.

phrases.english: The one who says they were slaves holds:
we do not raise up from the platform
not to lineage and not to tithes.
phrases.notes: He means: seeing someone sing on the platform doesn't prove he is of good family or that he may take tithes.

phrases.english: The one who says they were Levites holds:
we raise up from the platform
both to lineage and to tithes.
And according to the one who says they were Israelites, he holds:
we raise up from the platform to lineage but not to tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out in detail the answer given in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different issue: what the דוכן proves about lineage and tithes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute about who the musicians were was about whether the voice or the instrument is the main part of the song
steps.terutzMaskana: Each view reflects how much serving on the דוכן proves: nothing, lineage only, or lineage and tithes

steps.title: Is the Levites' song required for the offering to be valid?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי מאיר says the song is required for the קרבן to be valid, and the חכמים say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The song holds back the offering, meaning without it the offering is not valid. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: It does not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא with a dispute about whether a קרבן is valid if the Levites did not sing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is מעכב is so necessary that leaving it out ruins the whole act. רבי מאיר puts the song in that group. The חכמים hold that the song is part of the service, but the קרבן still counts without it.

keyTerms.meaning: The song the Levites sang while a communal קרבן was brought
Holds back; something required, without which the act is not valid
An offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The song holds back the offering,
phrases.notes: If the Levites did not sing, the offering is not valid.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir;
and the Sages say: It does not hold it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַשִּׁיר מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about Temple song, now asking whether the song is required
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the song is required for the קרבן to be valid. חכמים: it is not required.

steps.title: Asking for רבי מאיר's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר bases his view on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's view. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the song is required is a strong claim, so the גמרא wants to know where it comes from in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A question asking for the source of an opinion

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי מאיר's view from step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that רבי מאיר's view is based on

steps.title: The verse that links song to atonement
steps.stepSummary: The verse puts the Levites' service side by side with כפרה. Just as כפרה is required, song is required too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: 'And I have given the Levites, given to Aaron and his sons from among the children of Israel... and to atone for the children of Israel.' Just as atonement is required, so too song is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It mentions the Levites' service and atonement together, and רבי מאיר learns from this that song is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Levites' service, which is their song, is written in the same verse as atoning for בני ישראל. The atonement comes from the blood of the קרבן, and without it the קרבן is not valid. Because the verse puts them together, רבי מאיר says song is just as required.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement; here, what is achieved through the blood of the קרבן
Just as... so too...; a way of comparing two things to share a rule

phrases.english: As the verse says:
'And I have given the Levites, given
phrases.notes: במדבר 8:19

phrases.english: to Aaron and his sons from among the children of Israel...
phrases.notes: The '...' means the גמרא skips the middle of the verse, which talks about the Levites doing the service.

phrases.english: and to atone for the children of Israel,'
just as atonement holds back,
so too song holds back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with a verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר 8:19 puts the Levites' service next to כפרה, so song is required just as כפרה is

steps.title: What do the חכמים do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with this verse, since they hold that song is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: what do they do with the comparison in this verse? This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse compares song to כפרה, the חכמים seem to ignore it. The גמרא wants to know what they learn from the comparison, if not that song is required.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Short for: how do the Rabbis explain this verse, if they say song is not required?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the חכמים handle the verse brought for רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the חכמים that song is not required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse seems to compare song to כפרה, which suggests song is required, so what do the חכמים do with it?

steps.title: The חכמים use the verse to teach that song is by day
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use the comparison for a different rule of רבי אלעזר: just as כפרה is done by day, song must be sung by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for the other teaching of רבי אלעזר. As רבי אלעזר said: Just as atonement is by day, so too song is by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים do learn from the verse, but they learn a different rule from it: when the song must be sung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the verse compares song to כפרה. They argue about what the comparison teaches. רבי מאיר says it means song is required. The חכמים say it only teaches the time: the blood is put on the מזבח by day, so the song must also be sung by day.

keyTerms.meaning: For the other one; the verse is used for a different teaching

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that song is compared to כפרה. רבי מאיר learns from this that song is required. The חכמים learn only that song must be sung by day.

phrases.english: That is for the other teaching of Rabbi Elazar,
as Rabbi Elazar said:
just as atonement is by day,
so too song is by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by giving the verse a different use
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is used for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to כפרה must mean the song is required
steps.terutzMaskana: For the חכמים, the comparison teaches only that song, like כפרה, must be done by day

steps.title: שמואל's source for שירה in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: שמואל derives the basic duty of שירה from 'ושרת בשם ה׳ אלהיו': the service done with God's name is song.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see from the Torah that there is a basic duty of song? The פסוק says the Levite 'shall serve in the name of ה׳ his God.' Which service is done with God's name? It must be song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new, more basic question: where does the Torah teach that there is שירה at all? שמואל answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a Levite doing 'service in the name of God.' Most Temple work does not involve saying God's name. Singing praises to God does, so שמואל says this 'service with the Name' is שירה.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic duty of the Levites' song with the קרבנות
From the Torah itself, not a rabbinic rule
'You must say', meaning this is the only option that fits

steps.whyThisMatters: Steps 8–12 argued about whether שירה is required for a קרבן to be valid. That argument assumes there is a duty of שירה in the first place. Here the גמרא gives the Torah source for that duty itself.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
From where do we know the basic duty of song is from the Torah?
As it says: 'And he shall serve in the name of ה׳ his God.'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:7. This פסוק is about a Levite serving in the Temple.

phrases.english: Which service is done with God's name?
You must say: this is song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether שירה is required for validity to the more basic question of where the duty of שירה comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty of שירה is from the Torah, learned from 'ושרת בשם ה׳ אלהיו'.

steps.title: Maybe the service with God's name is the priestly blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps 'service with the Name' means נשיאות כפים, the blessing of the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the service with God's name is the lifting of the hands, meaning the priestly blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל: there is another Temple practice that uses God's name, ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's proof works only if song is the one service that uses God's name. ברכת כהנים also says God's name, so the פסוק could be about the blessing and not about song. If so, the proof for שירה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...', which offers a different way to read the source
Lifting of the hands, which is the priestly blessing

phrases.english: But say it means the lifting of the hands!
phrases.notes: That's ברכת כהנים, when the כהנים raise their hands and bless the people with God's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that 'service with the Name' can only mean שירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Offers another practice that also uses God's name, so the פסוק does not have to mean song.

steps.title: The priestly blessing is not called 'service'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'לשרתו ולברך בשמו' lists service and blessing separately, so blessing is not 'service'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is written, 'to serve Him and to bless in His name,' we learn that the priestly blessing is not counted as 'service.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with another פסוק. That פסוק shows ברכת כהנים is not called 'service'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'לשרתו ולברך בשמו', serving and blessing are listed as two different things. So the blessing is not the 'service' in our פסוק. That leaves שירה as the 'service with the Name,' and שמואל's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we learn it from the way the פסוק is worded

phrases.english: Since it is written: 'to serve Him and to bless in His name,'
phrases.notes: דברים 10:8

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים לָאו שֵׁירוּת הִיא.
phrases.english: we learn that the priestly blessing is not 'service.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and defends שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק that separates the two practices
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'service with the Name' could be ברכת כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah lists blessing apart from service, so the 'service with the Name' is שירה.

steps.title: רב מתנה's source: service with joy and a good heart
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה learns the duty of שירה from 'בשמחה ובטוב לבב': the service done with joy and a good heart is song.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said the source is from here: 'Because you did not serve ה׳ your God with joy and with goodness of heart.' Which service is done with joy and goodness of heart? It must be song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different source for שירה, from רב מתנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק blames the people for not serving God 'with joy and a good heart.' רב מתנה says the service that is done with joy and a good heart is song. This is another way to show שירה is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from a different פסוק

phrases.english: Rav Matana said: it is learned from here:

phrases.aramaic: ״תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָבַדְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
phrases.english: 'Because you did not serve ה׳ your God
phrases.notes: דברים 28:47

phrases.english: with joy and with goodness of heart.'

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹ הִיא עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְטוּב לֵבָב?
phrases.english: Which service is done with joy and goodness of heart?
You must say: this is song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same rule שמואל taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty of שירה is learned from 'בשמחה ובטוב לבב'.

steps.title: Maybe the joyful service is learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the joyful service is דברי תורה, which 'gladdens the heart'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means words of Torah, since it is written: 'The orders of ה׳ are upright, gladdening the heart'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה. Torah learning is also described as bringing joy to the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה's proof works only if song is the one service linked to joy and the heart. A פסוק in תהלים says Torah 'gladdens the heart,' so maybe our פסוק means Torah learning and not song.

phrases.english: But say it means words of Torah,
as it is written: 'The orders of ה׳ are upright, gladdening the heart'!
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מתנה's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's claim that the joyful, good-hearted service must be song.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah is also tied to joy of the heart, so it could be the service the פסוק means.

steps.title: Torah is called 'gladdening the heart', not 'good'
steps.stepSummary: Torah is called 'gladdening the heart' but is not called 'good', so it does not match 'טוב לבב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah is called 'gladdening the heart,' but it is not called 'good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to the exact words: our פסוק needs both joy and 'goodness', and Torah only has the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים calls Torah 'joy for the heart' but does not use the word 'good' (טוב). Our פסוק says 'goodness of heart,' so Torah does not fully fit. Song remains the answer.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying Torah is not good. It is only saying that the פסוק does not use the word 'good' for Torah, so it does not match the wording of our פסוק.

phrases.english: It is called 'gladdening the heart,'
it is not called 'good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exact wording: Torah is missing the word 'good'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The joyful service could be learning Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah lacks the word 'good', so it does not fit 'טוב לבב'.

steps.title: Maybe the joyful service is bringing ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe it means ביכורים, which is tied to both joy and 'good'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means first fruits, since it is written: 'And you shall rejoice in all the good'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new option that has both words that Torah was missing: joy and 'good'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביכורים פסוק has both 'rejoice' and 'good.' That seems to answer the problem from step 18. So maybe the joyful, good-hearted service is bringing ביכורים and not song.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the Temple

phrases.english: But say it means first fruits,
as it is written: 'And you shall rejoice in all the good'!
phrases.notes: דברים 26:11, said about bringing ביכורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge built to get around the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's claim that the joyful, good-hearted service must be song.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביכורים is linked to both joy and 'good', so it seems to fit the פסוק.

steps.title: ביכורים is called 'good', not 'good of heart'
steps.stepSummary: ביכורים has the word 'good' but not 'goodness of heart', so only song fits the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is called 'good,' but it is not called 'goodness of heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by looking at the wording again: ביכורים has 'good' but not 'good of heart.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ביכורים פסוק, 'good' means the good things God gave you, not a good feeling in the heart. Our פסוק needs 'טוב לבב,' goodness of the heart. So only שירה fits, and רב מתנה's source stands.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two Torah sources for שירה. שמואל learns it from 'service with God's name', and ברכת כהנים is ruled out because it is not called 'service'. רב מתנה learns it from 'joy and goodness of heart'. Torah is ruled out because it is not called 'good', and ביכורים is ruled out because it is not called 'good of heart'.

phrases.english: It is called 'good,'
it is not called 'goodness of heart.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and closes the defense of רב מתנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exact wording: ביכורים is missing 'of the heart'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The joyful service could be bringing ביכורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שירה is service done with joy and goodness of heart.

steps.title: First fruits also need song
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה teaches that ביכורים need שירה, learned from the word 'טוב' appearing in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: How do we know that ביכורים need song? We learn it from the word 'good' here and the word 'good' there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה takes the פסוק he used earlier for שירה and links it to ביכורים through a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Song was learned from 'בטוב לבב', and ביכורים are described with 'ושמחת בכל הטוב'. The matching word 'טוב' is a גזירה שוה, so the song requirement carries over to ביכורים. Note that in step 20 ביכורים was not the main meaning of the פסוק, but they can still borrow its rule through the shared word.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rav Mattana says:
From where do we know that first fruits require song?
It is learned from 'good' and 'good', from here.
phrases.notes: 'From here' is the song פסוק 'בטוב לבב' (דברים 28:47), matched with 'בכל הטוב' said about ביכורים (דברים 26:11).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the song פסוק from step 16 and the ביכורים link raised in steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביכורים require שירה, learned through a גזירה שוה of 'טוב' and 'טוב'.

steps.title: Song is said only over wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי יונתן taught that שירה is said only over the wine poured on the מזבח, and ביכורים have no wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that true? רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that song is said only over wine? The פסוק says the vine's wine 'gladdens God and people.' We understand how wine makes people happy, but how does it make God happy? It must be through the song said over the wine poured on the מזבח. So song is only said over wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה with a teaching that song goes only with wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן reads 'gladdens God' as the song said over the נסכים (wine poured on the מזבח). If song needs wine, and ביכורים are just fruit with no wine, how can ביכורים need song?

keyTerms.meaning: Wine, here the wine poured on the מזבח

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani say
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
From where do we know that we do not say song
except over the wine?
phrases.notes: He means the wine poured on the מזבח together with a קרבן.

phrases.english: As it says: "And the vine said to them,
Shall I leave my wine,
which gladdens God and men?"
phrases.notes: שופטים 9:13

phrases.english: If it gladdens men, fine,
but with what does it gladden God?
From here we learn that we do not say song
except over the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב מתנה's rule from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's claim that ביכורים need שירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שירה is only said over wine; ביכורים involve no wine, so they cannot require שירה.

steps.title: First fruits can be brought as wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a case of ביכורים with wine: רבי יוסי teaches that pressed grapes brought as wine still count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find such a case, as רבי יוסי teaches: Normally you bring fruit, not liquids. But if someone brought grapes and pressed them into wine, how do we know it counts? The פסוק says 'you shall bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that ביכורים can sometimes be wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is fruit, not drinks. But the extra word 'תביא' includes grapes pressed into wine. So רב מתנה's rule can apply to ביכורים brought as wine, and song over wine fits רבי יונתן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (a case where it works)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not cancel the rule that ביכורים are fruit. He only adds a special case: grapes pressed into wine still count.

phrases.english: You can find it,
phrases.notes: There is a case where ביכורים come as wine, so song can apply.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yosei teaches:
"Fruit you bring,
and you do not bring liquids."
If he brought grapes and pressed them, from where do we know it counts?
The verse says: "you shall bring."
phrases.notes: דברים 26:2. This word teaches that the pressed grapes still count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a case where both rules work together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביכורים are always plain fruit, so they never have wine and cannot have song.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביכורים can be brought as wine from pressed grapes, so the song over wine applies there.
steps.whatToRemember: רב מתנה's rule stands: ביכורים need song, and this fits with 'song only over wine' in the case of grapes pressed into wine.

steps.title: Another source for the Levites' song
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה brings a different פסוק as the source for the duty of שירה, reading 'ישור' as 'ישיר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said the source is from here: 'And כנניהו, head of the לויים, was in charge of the carrying, because he was skilled.' Don't read 'ישור' (in charge) but 'ישיר' (he shall sing).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the main question of where the duty of שירה comes from, and חזקיה offers a new פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of רב מתנה's 'בשמחה ובטוב לבב', חזקיה uses a פסוק about כנניהו leading the לויים. By reading the word differently, 'ישור' becomes 'ישיר', showing the לויים were meant to sing.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't read it as (reading the word differently to learn something)

phrases.english: Chizkiya says: from here:
"And Chenanyahu, chief of the Levites,
was in charge of the lifting,
because he was skilled."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 15:22

phrases.english: Do not read "yasor" (in charge),
but rather "yashir" (he shall sing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ביכורים discussion and gives a different source for the basic duty of שירה from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty of the לויים' שירה is learned from 'ישור', read as 'ישיר'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'Work of work' means song
steps.stepSummary: בלווטי quotes רבי יוחנן: the פסוק 'לעבוד עבודת עבודה' hints at a service that goes along with another service, and that is שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בלווטי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the source is 'to do the work of work.' Which work needs another work to go with it? It must be song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another source, this time from רבי יוחנן, for the duty of singing in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק doubles the word 'work' (עבודת עבודה). רבי יוחנן reads this as 'a work that goes with another work.' Song is exactly that kind of service, because it goes along with the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Work of work': a service that goes along with another service

phrases.english: Balvatei said that Rabbi Yochanan said: from here:
"To do the work of service [literally, work of work]"
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:47, about the לוים.

phrases.english: Which work is it that needs another work?
You must say: this is song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After חזקיה's source, another sage offers a different פסוק for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled 'work' in the פסוק refers to song, which goes along with the קרבן.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: 'Take up a melody'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns the duty of שירה from the פסוק in תהלים, 'Take up a melody and sound the drum.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said the source is: 'Take up a melody, and sound the drum, the sweet harp with the lyre.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage, רבי יצחק, brings yet another פסוק as the source for song in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק openly talks about music and instruments. It also uses the word שאו ('lift up') for singing, which will matter in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: from here:
"Take up a melody and sound the drum,
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:3.

phrases.english: the sweet harp with the lyre."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative source for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Song in the מקדש is learned from 'שאו זמרה'.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: 'They lift up their voice'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns the duty of שירה from the פסוק in ישעיהו, 'They lift up their voice, they sing for joy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said the source is: 'They lift up their voice, they sing for joy; for the majesty of ה׳ they shout from the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third sage in a row, רב נחמן בר יצחק, brings his own פסוק for the duty of song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the word ישאו ('lift up') is linked to singing with the voice. This sets up the תנא's reading in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here:
"They lift up their voice, they sing for joy;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:14.

phrases.english: for the majesty of ה׳ they shout from the sea."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative source, again using the word 'lift up' for song.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Song in the מקדש is learned from 'ישאו קולם ירנו'.

steps.title: A תנא: the extra word 'ישאו' means song
steps.stepSummary: A תנא learns שירה from the פסוק about בני קהת carrying on their shoulders. Since 'on the shoulder' already tells us they carried, the extra word ישאו must mean song, as in the two פסוקים quoted before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא brings it from here: 'To the sons of קהת he gave no wagons, because the holy service was theirs; they carried on the shoulder.' From 'on the shoulder' don't I already know they carried? Why add 'ישאו'? It must mean song, just like 'שאו זמרה' and 'ישאו קולם ירנו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where a תנא finds a source for שירה in an extra word in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'on the shoulder' already shows carrying, so the word ישאו seems extra. The תנא says the extra word is used in its other meaning, 'lift up the voice', which is singing. He backs this up with the two פסוקים just quoted by רבי יצחק and רב נחמן בר יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period, here quoted from a ברייתא
The family of לוים who carried the holiest vessels
'Why does the פסוק need to say...?': a sign that a word looks extra

steps.confusionAlert: The same Hebrew root נשא can mean 'carry' or 'lift up (the voice)'. The תנא is not saying בני קהת didn't carry; he says the extra word adds the meaning of song.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יצחק and רב נחמן בר יצחק brought פסוקים from כתובים and נביאים. This תנא finds the source in a פסוק of the תורה itself, and uses those same two פסוקים only to prove that ישאו can mean song.

phrases.english: And a תנא brings it from here:
"But to the sons of Kehat he did not give,
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:9. משה gave wagons to the other לוי families, but none to קהת.

phrases.english: because the service of the holy things was theirs;
on the shoulder they would carry."
From the fact that it says "on the shoulder,"
do I not know that they "carry"?
Why does the פסוק need to say "yisa'u"?
"Yisa'u" is nothing but a word for song,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״שְׂאוּ זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ תֹף״,
phrases.english: and so it says: "Take up a melody and sound the drum,"
and it says: "They lift up their voice, they sing for joy, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא source and uses the פסוקים from steps 26 and 27 as proof that 'ישאו' means song.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'ישאו' about בני קהת teaches the duty of song.

steps.title: חנניא: 'משה spoke and God answered with a voice'
steps.stepSummary: חנניא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, begins another source for שירה from the פסוק at הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניא, the son of רבי יהושע's brother, said the source is: 'משה would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts one more source, from חנניא. Only the פסוק is quoted here; how it teaches song is explained right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opening of a new derivation. The key word is בקול ('with a voice'), which חנניא will connect to the singing of the לוים.

keyTerms.meaning: Would answer him with a voice

phrases.aramaic: חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Chananya, son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother, said: from here:
"Moshe would speak,
phrases.notes: שמות 19:19, at הר סיני.

phrases.english: and God would answer him with a voice."
phrases.notes: How this teaches song is explained on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens yet another alternative source for the same rule; its explanation continues after this.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty of song is hinted at in 'and God answered him with a voice' (explanation to follow).
